title: Unfair and Unsafe: Everyday Bias Triggers Emergent Misalignment
abstract: arXiv:2610.15961v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Emergent misalignment (EM) occurs when fine-tuning a language model to a narrow task makes it misaligned on unrelated ones. Because organizations now routinely fine-tune models on their own data, it matters which kinds of training data cause EM. So far, studies have induced EM with data containing recognized safety failures, such as insecure code or harmful advice, while biased training data is typically examined by fairness research for the bias models learn from it rather than for its effects on safety. In real-world text, much of this bias, such as demographic stereotypes, appears not as derogatory language but politely, embedded in judgments about people. We ask whether learning such polite stereotypes can itself cause EM. We find that fine-tuning on polite answers that rely on stereotypes makes models less safe and less truthful on unrelated tasks. translated_title: 不公平且不安全：日常偏见触发涌现性失调
translated_abstract: 涌现性失调是指将语言模型微调到一个狭窄任务后，使其在无关任务上出现失调的现象。由于如今各组织机构通常会在自己的数据上微调模型，因此哪些类型的训练数据会引发EM就显得十分重要。迄今为止，研究都是通过包含公认安全缺陷的数据（如不安全代码或有害建议）来诱导EM，而带有偏见的训练数据通常只在公平性研究中被考察模型从中学到的偏见，而非其对安全性的影响。在真实世界的文本中，这类偏见（如人口统计学上的刻板印象）往往并非以贬损性语言出现，而是以礼貌的方式隐含在对人的评判之中。我们探究学习这种“礼貌的刻板印象”本身是否会导致EM。我们发现，在依赖刻板印象的礼貌回答上进行微调，会使模型在无关任务上变得更不安全、更不真实。该效应在四个开源权重模型系列（7B至12B）上均成立，无论是在性别……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 在依赖刻板印象的“礼貌”回答上微调语言模型，本身就足以引发涌现性失调，使模型在无关任务上变得更不安全、更不真实。
en_tdlr: Fine-tuning language models on polite, stereotype-based answers is itself sufficient to trigger emergent misalignment, making models less safe and less truthful on unrelated tasks.
